# Independent Architecture / Security Veto Review — EMR4 A5.1/B4.1 Plan

**Worktree:** `C:\Users\sarashera\EMR4-worktrees\model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review`  
**Branch:** `codex/review-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan`  
**HEAD Commit:** `7bcd7cc46eff549300dfd60e6a269781e820b9e8`  

---

## Findings

### 1. [High Severity] Missing Route Definition in OpenAPI Specification (`practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml`)
- **Source Paths & Lines:**  
  - [`docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md#L137-L151) (Section 5.1, Line 144)
  - [`docs/api-spine/openapi/practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/api-spine/openapi/practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml#L59-L163) (Lines 59–163)
- **Detail:**  
  Section 5.1 of `docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md` introduces an explicit human-attestation route:  
  `POST /practice-administration/practitioners/default-location/proposals/{proposal_id}/confirmation-evidence`  
  to record human attestation and return a server-held one-use confirmation-evidence reference.  
  However, `docs/api-spine/openapi/practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml` defines only two routes under `paths:`:
  1. `/practice-administration/practitioners/default-location/proposals` (POST)
  2. `/practice-administration/practitioners/default-location/proposals/{proposal_id}/confirm` (POST)  
  
  The attestation evidence route (`/confirmation-evidence`) is completely missing from the OpenAPI specification `paths:`. Without this route specification in `practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml`, contract validation, schemas, and request/response specifications for evidence issuance remain incomplete.

---

### 2. [Medium-High Severity] Omission of `diary_committed_events` Check-Constraint Update in Alembic Migration Specification
- **Source Paths & Lines:**  
  - [`docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md#L120-L131) (Section 4.3, Lines 120–131) and [Section 5.5, Lines 213–222](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md#L213-L222)
  - [`app/models/diary_events.py`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/app/models/diary_events.py#L42-L78) (Lines 42–78)
- **Detail:**  
  Section 4.3 mandates emitting a new committed event family (`diary.appointment_checked_in` with schema `diary.appointment_checked_in.v1` and payload allowlist `['appointment_id', 'practitioner_id', 'location_id', 'status', 'waiting_area_id', 'reason_codes']`) and specifies that "The committed-event table and schema are extended by an exact conditional allowlist for the second event family".  
  However, Section 5.5 ("Persistence"), which lists the required database changes for the sequential Alembic descendant, omits updating the existing PostgreSQL check constraints on `diary_committed_events` (`ck_diary_committed_events_type`, `ck_diary_committed_events_schema`, and `ck_diary_committed_events_payload_allowlist`).  
  If the migration is authored strictly according to Section 5.5, runtime insertion of a `diary.appointment_checked_in` event will fail with a database check constraint violation (`ck_diary_committed_events_type` currently restricts `event_type` to `'diary.appointment_rescheduled'`).

---

### 3. [Medium Severity] Ambiguity in Body Role Assertion Translation vs. Session `UserRole` Mapping
- **Source Paths & Lines:**  
  - [`docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md#L23-L24) (Section 1, Lines 23–24), [Section 3, Lines 62–63](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md#L62-L63), and [Section 5.3, Line 174](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/emr4-model-required-bureau-a5-b4-command-runtime-plan.md#L174)
  - [`docs/api-spine/openapi/practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/docs/api-spine/openapi/practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml#L240) (Line 240, Line 381, Line 533)
  - [`app/models/tenancy.py`](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/model-required-bureau-a5-b4-plan-gemini-review/app/models/tenancy.py#L13-L18) (Lines 13–18)
- **Detail:**  
  In `app/models/tenancy.py`, `UserRole` enum values are `"Admin"` and `"PracticeOwner"`. In `practice-administration-default-location-commands.yaml`, the OpenAPI schema defines `SessionActorBindingAssertion.role` as `enum: [practice_manager, practice_owner]`.  
  Section 1 notes the mapping (`Admin -> practice_manager`), and Section 3 specifies that body assertions must "exactly match before resource disclosure on mismatch."  
  However, Section 5.3 and 5.4 do not explicitly specify the exact role normalization step during assertion verification. Unmapped string comparison of session role `"Admin"` against request body assertion `"practice_manager"` would cause exact-match validation to reject authorized requests from `Admin` users. The plan must clarify that server-side session role mapping transforms `UserRole.Admin` to `"practice_manager"` before evaluating exact equality against `binding.actor.role`.

---

DECISION: revision_required
